instruction: Access the recreation.gov homepage and confirm the URL starts with 'https://www.recreation.gov'.

metadata.explanation: Similar to variation 4 but uses the approximate matching function (is_expected_active_tab_approximate) which ignores query parameters. This allows for more flexible URL matching while still verifying navigation to the correct site. Uses existing Chrome metrics.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic mismatch between instruction and evaluator logic
Instruction says "URL starts with https://www.recreation.gov" (prefix match), but evaluator performs exact URL equality check (after stripping query params)
The metric is_expected_active_tab_approximate uses exact equality (strip_query(expected_url) == strip_query(actual_url)) instead of startswith check
If agent navigates to any subpage of recreation.gov (e.g., /search, /camping/...), the instruction would consider it valid (starts with the base URL), but the evaluator would fail it
This creates a semantic gap where correct task completion may be incorrectly evaluated as failed
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Option 1: Change the metric to use startswith check instead of exact equality to match the "starts with" semantics in the instruction
Option 2: Update the instruction to say "confirm the URL is exactly https://www.recreation.gov/" to match the exact equality behavior of the evaluator
Recommended: Option 1 is better as it matches the original instruction intent and allows verification of navigation to the recreation.gov domain (including subpages)
